summary: Self-hosted memory hub for agent teams that saves chat memory, reusable skills, document wikis and code maps so the next agent doesn't start from zero.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: TencentDB Agent Memory is a memory hub for AI agents. It extracts chat memory and reusable skills from conversations, turns documents into a linked wiki and code into a CodeGraph, and shares them across agents and team members. Agents connect through a proxy by pointing their base URL at it.
sixtySeconds.problem: Agents forget project context between sessions and every new agent re-reads the same docs and code. This keeps that knowledge and hands it to the next agent.
whoFor: Claude Code, OpenClaw, Hermes or OpenCode users
People who want self-hosted agent memory
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for memory that isn't tied to one agent framework, with chat memory, skills, wiki and code graph in one panel.
requirements: LLM API settings for the memory and proxy services

overview: One script starts three services: memory-core, memory-hub and a proxy. You fill in two sets of LLM settings in .env first, one for memory processing and one for the proxy.

Agents such as Claude Code, Hermes and OpenClaw connect through the proxy with a user key; most need no plugin, hook or MCP server. The panel at localhost:8125 lets you review and edit memories and skills.
Memory is layered from raw conversations up to scenarios and personas, and sharing is controlled by session bindings and permissions. Full deployment docs are in INSTALL.md.
